introduction.text: Forte Boccea is one of Rome’s 15 forts, built between 1877 and 1891 as part of the city’s entrenched field. The fort later served as a military remand prison and is now being converted into a cultural park.

history.description: Construction of Forte Boccea began in 1877 and was completed in 1881, covering an area of 7.3 hectares at the first kilometre of Via di Boccea.
General Mario Carloni was held as a prisoner in the fort from 1946 to 19 May 1951.
In 2013, a resolution approved the conversion of Forte Boccea into a park for cultural initiatives.
After its completion, the fort functioned as a military remand prison until 2005.
